slides.headline: What is a working capital loan?
slides.body: Working capital loans fund the operational engine of a business — inventory, payroll, rent and overheads — rather than a specific asset. Structured around your revenue cycle, funds may be drawn as a lump sum or in tranches, giving flexibility to manage day-to-day costs as they arise.

caption:
Payroll doesn't wait for a slow month, and neither does rent.

Working capital loans are built to fund the everyday running of a business — stock, staffing, overheads — structured around your revenue cycle rather than tied to a single asset. Facilities can often be drawn as a lump sum or in tranches, and structured as revolving or term finance depending on what suits.

Want to see what a facility built around your cycle looks like? Get in touch.
